discovery: Realization of strongly interacting fermionic superfluids and the BEC-BCS crossover in ultracold atomic gases

nominees.name: Rudolf Grimm
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Christophe Salomon
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire Kastler Brossel, Ecole Normale Superieure, Paris, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / ultracold quantum gases
motivation: Using Feshbach resonances in ultracold lithium-6 gases, the nominees turned the decades-old theoretical idea of a continuous crossover between Bose-Einstein condensation of tightly bound molecules and BCS pairing of fermions into a controllable laboratory reality. Grimm's group produced long-lived weakly bound molecules and among the first molecular Bose-Einstein condensates (2003), then measured collective modes and the pairing gap across the crossover. Salomon's group pioneered Feshbach molecule formation and precision thermodynamics of the unitary Fermi gas, establishing universal equations of state. Zwierlein, in the MIT effort and later at the helm of his own group, gave the decisive proof of superfluidity through vortex lattices throughout the crossover and later measured the superfluid transition of the unitary gas. Together these works created a universal, tunable model system for strongly correlated fermions, connecting superconductors, neutron stars and quark-gluon plasma, and seeding today's fermionic quantum simulation.
